one_liner: Header-only C++11 FFT (multi-D, any length, DCT/DST) behind NumPy and SciPy; about 4.5x faster than KissFFT on 3D transforms.
what_it_does: A single header, pocketfft_hdronly.h, with templated c2c, r2c, c2r, r2r (FFTPACK half-complex and Hartley), DCT and DST types I-IV. It works on strided N-dimensional arrays with chosen axes, in float, double or long double. Calls are one-shot functions that take shape, byte strides, axes, a scale factor and a thread count. There is no plan object, and the API is not compatible with KissFFT or FFTW.
how_it_is_fast: The core is a heavily reworked FFTPACK with radix codelets for 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 11 (complex) and 2, 3, 4, 5 (real), plus Bluestein's algorithm so large-prime lengths stay O(N log N). For multi-D or batched transforms it runs several 1D lines at once using GCC/Clang vector_size types (SSE2, AVX, AVX-512, NEON, VSX, RISC-V V), and it splits the work across an internal pthread thread pool. Twiddle factors take only about 2*sqrt(n) sin/cos calls, so plan setup is cheap (1274 ns vs FFTW's 25610 ns at n=512 in the gemmi benchmark).
when_to_use: 2D/3D real or complex FFTs on strided or non-contiguous arrays, e.g. crystallography grids or image volumes
Arbitrary lengths, including large primes, where FFTW's GPL or KissFFT's speed is a problem
Workloads with many different sizes, where FFTW's plan time dominates (very fast setup)
Projects that want one BSD header with DCT/DST and float/double/long double support
Matching NumPy/SciPy FFT results in C++ code
when_not_to_use: Single short 1D transforms: the 1D path is not vectorized (4009 ns vs FFTW 588 ns and pffft 1255 ns at n=512 complex in gemmi's run, though that row used the older C version)
Peak 3D throughput on Intel: MKL 2019 measured 61 ms vs 97 ms for 256^3 R2C
Compilers other than GCC/Clang >= 5: MSVC and ICC get no SIMD (vectorization is gated on GCC/Clang)
Windows multithreading: it uses pthreads (open issue #2 asks for a Windows pool)
You need versioned releases: none are tagged (open issue #24)

integration.min_toolchain: C++11; SIMD needs GCC >= 5 or Clang >= 5 (AppleClang >= 9.1)
integration.platforms: any C++11 platform; SIMD on x86 SSE2/AVX/AVX-512, ARM NEON, POWER VSX, RISC-V V via compile-time flags such as -march=native
integration.thread_safety: Free functions; the optional plan cache (POCKETFFT_CACHE_SIZE) and thread pool are mutex-protected; the nthreads argument sets parallelism for multi-D transforms

gotchas: Strides are in bytes, not elements; r2c/c2r cannot be done in place
Transforms are unnormalized: pass the scale via fct
The plan cache is off by default (POCKETFFT_CACHE_SIZE=0); turn it on for repeated short 1D transforms, but it can use a lot of memory for large lengths
Errors throw C++ exceptions (std::runtime_error, invalid_argument, bad_alloc); there is a reported aligned_alloc build failure on Android/Termux clang (issue #23)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick PocketFFT over pffft and muFFT for multi-dimensional data, arbitrary lengths, double/long double, or DCT/DST. Pick pffft or muFFT for SIMD-accelerated short 1D transforms of 5-smooth or power-of-two sizes.
verified_claims_summary: In project-gemmi's benchmarking-fft (GCC 8 -O3, i7-5600U, float, KissFFT scalar), the PocketFFT cpp branch with AVX did a 256^3 R2C in 97 ms vs KissFFT 436 ms (4.5x, derived) and 416x256x416 in 311 ms vs 2078 ms, matching FFTW measured from Ubuntu binaries (98 ms). The 3D C2C 256^3 run (SSE) took 264 ms vs KissFFT 785 ms but FFTW measured 162 ms.
status_note: Active (commits through mid-2026); this GitHub fork mirrors the canonical gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/mtr/pocketfft cpp branch; BSD-3-Clause single header, easy to vendor.
